facts: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14; below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.
Lemon juice is about pH 2; pure water is pH 7; bleach is about pH 12 to 13.
pH = −log10[H+]; each pH unit is a tenfold change.

narration.text: Acids and bases are two families of chemicals, measured on the pH scale.
A pH below seven means acidic, like lemon juice.
Pure water is neutral, with a pH of seven.
Above seven is basic, also called alkaline, like soap.
Lemon juice is strongly acidic, about pH two.
Pure water sits right in the middle at seven.
Bleach is strongly basic, around pH twelve.
When an acid meets a base, they react together.
This reaction is called neutralisation.
It produces a salt and water.
Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide make table salt and water.
pH is the negative log of the hydrogen ion concentration.
Zero point zero zero one is ten to the minus three.
So the pH is three, which is acidic.
Each step of one pH unit is a tenfold change in acidity.

narration.text: Acids taste sour, while bases taste bitter. Never taste chemicals in the lab!
Acids have a pH below seven, and bases above seven.
Acids turn blue litmus paper red.
Lemon juice is an acid, and soap is a base.
